title: AWS Lambda: Invocation, Concurrency & Event Sources
summary: How Lambda is triggered, scales and fails, and the controls that keep it reliable.
tldr: Three invocation styles: **synchronous** (API Gateway, function URL: the caller handles errors), **asynchronous** (S3, SNS, EventBridge: Lambda queues and retries), and **event source mapping** (SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams, MSK: Lambda polls in batches).

Control scale with **reserved concurrency** (cap and guarantee for one function) or, for SQS, the event source mapping's **maximum concurrency** (cap pollers without throttling messages into the DLQ).
Release safely with **versions** and **aliases**. An alias can split traffic by weight between two versions and be switched back instantly.

keyFacts.text: Maximum function timeout. Memory goes up to 10,240 MB (CPU scales with it) and `/tmp` ephemeral storage up to 10,240 MB.
Lambda retries a failed **asynchronous** invocation up to twice by default. Then an **on-failure destination** or DLQ keeps the event; destinations also record the error.
For Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams, **BisectBatchOnFunctionError**, `MaximumRetryAttempts` and an on-failure destination stop one bad record from blocking a shard.
The **parallelization factor** (up to 10) processes several batches per Kinesis or DynamoDB shard at once, while keeping order per partition key.
A VPC-connected function runs in the subnets you give it. Configure subnets in **at least two AZs** so an AZ failure doesn't stop it.

keywords.cue: SQS consumer must not exceed 20 concurrent calls, don't send valid messages to the DLQ
keywords.answer: Maximum concurrency on the SQS event source mapping

keywords.cue: async EventBridge-triggered function must stay under a concurrency limit without losing events
send successful results to EventBridge and failures to a queue, no code
one bad record blocks a Kinesis or DynamoDB stream shard
keywords.answer: BisectBatchOnFunctionError plus retry limit and on-failure destination

keywords.cue: Kinesis iterator age grows but stream throughput is fine
send 10% of traffic to a new version, roll back instantly
only a specific SNS topic or S3 bucket may invoke the function
simple HTTPS endpoint for one cross-account role, no API Gateway features
No space left on device for large files
idle EC2 instance polls S3 for new uploads

traps: Reserved concurrency on an SQS-triggered function throttles pollers and can push valid messages to the DLQ; use maximum concurrency instead.
Provisioned concurrency is not a limit. It pre-warms environments and still lets the function scale beyond it.
An asynchronous-invocation DLQ does nothing for event source mappings; streams use the mapping's on-failure destination.
A longer timeout or larger batch size makes a poison-record problem worse, not better.
Lambda can't run longer than 15 minutes. Long jobs belong on Fargate, Batch or a Step Functions workflow.
